topic: Mutual Fund and ETF Fees and Expenses
source_evidence: When you purchase shares that have a back-end sales load instead of a front-end sales load, no sales load is deducted at the time of your purchase.
question: Misconception: A back-end sales load is deducted when you buy mutual fund shares, reducing the amount invested at the start.
answer: A back-end sales load is generally paid when you redeem (sell back) your shares, not when you purchase them. If no other purchase fees or charges apply, all of your money is used to buy shares initially; the back-end load is later taken from the money you receive when you exit the fund.
